utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, would you please have the accused brought in? (Accused enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (No translation). Is everything all right? Can you hear me? GENERAL BLASKIC: Good morning, your Honours. I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to repeat just for our schedule that tomorrow, Thursday, there will not be a hearing because the room is going to be occupied and also there is a plenary session of the judges in the afternoon. As regards Friday, we will sit on Friday morning, partly for the same reasons. I would also like to say, because it is now official, that as the weeks come there should be fewer complications in the courtroom, since a new courtroom -- I am looking to be sure I am saying the right thing at the Registrar -- a new courtroom will be built quickly and perhaps there might even be a third one. Therefore we are experiencing some delay right now. My colleagues and I want to encourage you to get to the essentials every time there is an examination and a cross-examination, but we might then be able to catch up -- make up for the delays. So does everybody understand that now? Yes. Therefore, we can resume our work now. I give the floor to the Prosecution, that is Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, your Honours, counsel. Your Honour, I would like to call Mr. Simon Leach back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, would you have the usher bring in Mr. Simon Leach, please? (Witness enters court) Mr. Simon Leach (continued) Examined by Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Simon Leach, please be seated. You are under oath already and therefore we do not have to ask you to take the oath again. Where were we, Mr. Harmon, in the questioning of Mr. Simon Leach? We were interrupted for organisational matters. Could you recall where we are before we continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we were -- Mr. Leach was testifying about Vitez. At the conclusion of his testimony I moved to introduce two exhibits. There were objections to the introduction of those two exhibits and I informed the court that I would return to those exhibits when I started, and I intend to do so at this time. So if we could have, your Honour, exhibits 30, 30A and 30B, then I can start with that exhibit and Mr. Leach can testify about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me for a moment and after that I promise I won't interrupt you any further. About how long do you think you are going to need to complete your examination? Then I will ask Mr. Hayman and Mr. Nobilo how long they are planning for so that we can organise the work properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I intend to finish with Mr. Leach today. It is difficult, depending on the number of potential objections, if any. I would anticipate I would finish with Mr. Leach by late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Not knowing what testimony is to come today, your Honour, it's difficult. Based on the testimony that Mr. Leach has given so far, I would estimate under an hour of cross, if that; perhaps under half an hour, but again I do not know what's to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, of course but I understand that I'm going to ask for each of the witnesses not so that you are prevented from saying what you want to say, but in order for us to maintain a strict schedule. I understand that one cannot say exactly how long it's going to take, but we can assume that the testimony of Mr. Leach will be concluded by Friday morning. Today will be devoted to the questioning by Mr. Harmon and then on Friday morning you think perhaps you will be finished perhaps even before the morning break. Of course we will operate in respect of what the witness says. I give you the floor, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If we could have Exhibits 30, 30A and 30B returned to the easel, then I'll start my examination of Mr. Leach. All right, Mr. Leach. Could you just refresh my recollection and the court's recollection of what that exhibit is and what it represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a map produced by Shell Multi Company. It's a 1:250,000 map of the Netherlands. On it there are two overlays. The first one to the bottom left-hand corner is the three municipalities of Vitez, Busovaca and Kiseljak, which are inverted. The larger overlay at the top right-hand corner is the Central Bosnia operative zone. In orange are highlighted the municipalities again of Vitez, Busovaca and Kiseljak and then to the top left-hand area you will see an area that's shaded by a series of lines. That was the municipality of Jajce, which fell to the Bosnian Serb army around November of 1992 and thereafter fell outside the operative command area of General Blaskic at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, there was a question when we left this exhibit last time, as to whether the scale of the map of the Netherlands was the same as the scale of the overlays?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. What has been done is that the opstina boundaries came from a map which was 1:500,000, i.e. twice as small as the shell map. That overlay has been created by increasing the size of the opstina boundary material on a photocopying machine by copying it at 200 per cent. Therefore, the scale for the overlays matches the scale for the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, your Honour, I would move to introduce Exhibit 30A and 30B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Weren't these already put into the record?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Well, they were presented but not yet admitted by the Trial Chamber, because the Defence had expressed an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you had expressed your objection. Do you continue to object or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I would intend to question the witness about the photocopy enlargement, because I never trust those 150 per cent and 200 per cent items, but I think the court can admit them and I can go into that on cross, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me remind you that in general in this Trial Chamber the three judges have agreed that almost all exhibits will be put into the record and each of the parties will argue as to the credibility of those exhibits. However, of course, there could be exceptions, which is why I asked the question. So theoretically in any case we will accept these maps as exhibits. Under what numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be 30, 30A for the overlap and 30B for the little map which the witness is holding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you go on, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Now, your Honour, I'll turn to exhibits 29, 29A, 29B and 29C. There was an objection to those exhibits being entered into evidence. If I could have 29A, 29B and 29C placed on the easel, then I could proceed. Mr. President, the objection that had been raised to this particular exhibit was the village of Sivrino Selo was marked in orange. It was available for counsel to inspect. It has been changed. I am informed it has been changed by the Registrar's office. If counsel is satisfied with the changes, then I would seek to introduce this particular exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: May we look at it, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. (Pause.)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It looks fine, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Therefore we'll accept this into the record. Fine. It will be under what number, Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 29, 29A for the first overlay with the concentric circles, 29B for the second and 29C for the little map, which was also changed, and which is on the witness bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Leach, I would ask you to keep the small maps with the concentric circles -- I think it is 29C and D -- with you at your witness stand, because I'm going to be asking you a number of questions about those. Returning to the large exhibit, Mr. Leach could you refresh the court's recollection as to what the centre point of each of those two sets of concentric circles represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will have to realign them. Just one moment, please. (Pause.)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer my question, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The concentric circles, the exhibit to the top left-hand corner of the main map is centred on the Hotel Vitez. The second overlay with concentric circles is centred on the barracks at Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the significance of each of those locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are both -- the Hotel Vitez in Vitez was the main command of General Blaskic and there was also a command at Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now referring to the large map, Mr. Leach, after the HVO launched attacks in that area on 16th April, did the Armija, the army of the Muslims, cut the road between those two areas represented by the concentric circles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did, your Honours. There was Armija control of areas from an area known as Kacuni down the Kiseljak road past the area called Bilalovac. I'll indicate that on the road now. That area there is Kacuni (indicating) and in this region here is the area which -- this region here was in the control of the Armija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, I would like to return --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting. I had understood this witness' testimony was in the nature of a percipient witness, not an expert. Could I enquire was I wrong? Is this witness being offered as an expert in that he is testifying clearly to matters either of a summary nature or certainly far outside his own personal knowledge. If he is being tendered as an expert, that will affect our preparation for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, he is not being tendered as an expert. He is indicating particular locations on physical exhibits on maps. We could have marked the map with that particular location. He could have testified about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I have no difficulty with him identifying any number of locations. It is simply when he adds other commentary about events that happened in 1992 or 1993 that are not based on his personal knowledge. Then that will require me on cross to perhaps go into matters at greater length than were necessary than if he would limit his answers to the type that counsel is describing. That's all, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In general, Mr. Hayman, we cannot interrupt a witness. If a prosecution witness answers in such a way that when you ask questions in cross-examination, that's one thing, but he has not really yet begun to ask questions of the Prosecutor. You are already thinking ahead about what will be your handicap during cross-examination. I think this is not something which would help move the proceedings along. I do not sustain your objection and I ask the Prosecutor to continue asking his questions. You will make decisions as to your own strategy as you feel necessary, and if you need some more time, the Trial Chamber will give that time to you. Therefore, please, let us allow the examination by the Prosecutor to continue. Mr. Harmon, please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honours, when Mr. Leach also concluded his testimony the last time, he had introduced Exhibit 32, which was a map of the Vitez town plan, and Exhibit 33, which was a photo album containing 11 photos of Vitez. Could I have Exhibit 32, please, shown to Mr. Leach again? Mr. Leach, just to return briefly to this exhibit, what does that exhibit represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a town plan of the town of Vitez, in Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that map illustrate all of the buildings that are located in Vitez itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, your Honour, I would now offer as my next exhibit a large -- a series of large photographs. I would like to have the usher present these photographs to the Registrar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is the photo album?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, your Honour. This is an entirely new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There is in the course of -- your Honour, there are five copies of this exhibit. There is one photograph original for the exhibit itself, one original photograph for your Honours and two photocopies, and a photocopy for defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let's go on, please, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, can you identify that exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's an aerial photograph of the main area and town of Vitez and Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the source of that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The photograph was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by the British Ministry of Defence in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that pursuant to Rule 70?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date that the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was taken on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've been to Vitez a number of occasions; that is correct, in Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many occasions approximately have you been to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten, fifteen, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had had an opportunity to examine this particular exhibit before you came into court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that photograph accurately show the town of Vitez and the structures that are identified on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As regards 9th November 1994, I would say that is probably an accurate portrayal. Since that photograph was taken there has obviously been some reconstruction of damaged property and new property has been constructed in certain areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you get into a description of that, Mr. Leach, your Honour, I would move to introduce this photograph into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, do you have any objections? All right. It will be placed into the record.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, would you begin describing the various buildings? There is a legend on the upper left-hand corner of that. Would you just take us through the legend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number A -- sorry, letter A on the legend is the Hotel Vitez itself (indicating). The A is actually situated where I would say the main entrance to the hotel is from the road. Letter B is the -- what I would call the Cinema complex, which is just to the right of the letter B and is almost a T-shaped building. Those two buildings are joined (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a military headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, part of that building was the headquarters of the military commander at the time, Mario Cerkez. Letter C is the PTT building, which is the telecommunications building for national telephone lines and international telephone calls. Letter D is the situation of the Chess Club in Vitez. That location will become more apparent to your Honours during the testimony of other witnesses (indicating). Letter E --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Where is D exactly? Where it D?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: D. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Letter E is an indication of the approximate location of the confrontation line, the front line, which developed after the morning attacks on the 16th April (indicating). Letter F is the location of the mosque in Stari Vitez (indicating). Letter G is the location of a large grave site, where Muslim civilians were buried after their bodies were collected after the attacks on 16th April (indicating). Letter H is the approximate location where a truck filled with explosives exploded in the Main Street into Stari Vitez on 19th April 1993 (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean letter I?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apologies. Yes, letter I. (Indicating). Going back to letter H, that's the location of a Bosnian army headquarters in Stari Vitez (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Your Honours, I would like to move to my next exhibit. Mr. Leach, can you identify this exhibit, please, and explain to the court what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The front page of the exhibit, your Honours, it a photocopy of this document here. This is a book produced in Zagreb, Croatia, which details the ethnic composition and census figures for The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991. The second page is a breakdown of relevant figures for the three municipalities of Busovaca, Vitez and Kiseljak. The remaining pages, which are in A3 size, are the copies for those municipalities photocopied from the book I have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce Exhibit 46 into evidence. Your Honour, now I would like to move to the Ahmici phase of the evidence. We concluded in large part with that on the last occasion. I would now like to return to that. Mr. Leach, referring to Exhibit 46, can you tell me what the 1991 census figures were in respect of the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The figures for Ahmici were a total number of 466. The Bosnian Muslims were 356. Bosnian Croats were 87. Yugoslavs were 2. Mixed origins were 21.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now do the figures of 1991 -- were they the same, to your knowledge, as the number of Muslims living in Ahmici in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. My understanding is that there were a number of refugees using houses in Ahmici in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge are there any Muslims living in Ahmici today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now what is the distance again from the Hotel Vitez to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's 4.8 kms by road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much time does that take to get to by car from the Hotel Vitez to Ahmici itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under normal driving conditions on a normal road, driving at safe, normal speed, about seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the usher could present the next exhibit. Mr. Leach, can you identify that exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a selection of photographs that were taken in May 1996. I was present when the photographs were taken. They were taken by two officers from the Dutch national police. They are a selection of photographs from the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do those photographs accurately represent the conditions of the buildings on 26th May 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do the photographs contained in that particular exhibit represent photographs of all of the buildings that were destroyed in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they do not. This is a selection of photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would move to introduce Exhibit 47, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the whole booklet is number 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Because there is a little label on the bottom that says 47. That's the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: For clarification there are numbers marked on each of the photographs. In the course of Mr. Leach's evidence he is going to refer to certain number of those that are marked. Why don't we do that? Mr. Leach, would you please refer to P47? Could you place that on the ELMO? I'm not sure the ELMO is on. There it is. All right. Can you explain what that photograph is, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a photograph of the lower mosque in Ahmici. One can see the minaret, which is tilted and has been blown up from the main part of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does that main mosque sit in relation to the road that goes from Vitez to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's approximately 150-200 metres from the main road. One can quite clearly see it from the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Leach, could you now turn to photograph P114 and place that on the ELMO and explain what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a much closer picture of the lower mosque in Ahmici, taken from just a few feet, 10, 15 feet. There's a road that passes the mosque. Again you can see the structure of the minaret in the centre picture just to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Leach, will you turn to PH77? Would you explain what that photograph represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again this is another photograph taken from very close by the building, 10, 15 feet away. This is the upper mosque in Ahmici. This mosque did not have a minaret attached to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many mosques were there in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you now turn to Exhibit PH78 and place that on the ELMO? Again what is that, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Taken from the road next to it that runs past it, that's again the upper mosque in Ahmici taken from another side angle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also turn to PH79 now and place that on the ELMO. Could you explain what that photograph represents, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is again the upper mosque in Ahmici photographed from the south side, I would say. The first photograph was from the north, the next photograph was from adjacent to the mosque. We have now moved further down the road and are looking back up towards the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you next turn to photograph PH109? What does that photograph represent, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a photograph of the school in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that school in relation to the main road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again that's approximately 200 metres from the main road. If you are driving to Ahmici, it's to the left of the road that goes into Ahmici, very close to the lower mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Leach, now the other photographs that are contained in Prosecutor's Exhibit 47 show a number of damaged or destroyed houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then I would like to conclude with that particular exhibit, Mr. Leach, and once it's reassembled, we will proceed with your examination. Mr. Leach, one final question in respect of that exhibit. I may not have made myself perfectly clear in my question. The damaged houses depicted in Prosecutor's Exhibit 47 are houses that are damaged in the village of Ahmici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, I would like to move into date order to some, but not all, of the villages that were attacked in the Lasva Valley on 16th April 1993. I would like to start with the village of Santici. If you would be so kind as to place map 29C, which is the map of Vitez with concentric circles on the ELMO, the small map. All right. I am going to ask you to point to something. I am not sure I can do that with the current state of the exhibit. All right. First of all, I would like to turn to Santici. Mr. Leach, can you use your pointer and show the court where Santici is located on that particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Mr. Leach, could you now refer to the census figures and inform the court what the 1991 census were for the village of Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population was 1008. Of that, 193 were Bosnian Muslims; 4 were Bosnian Serbs; 782 Bosnian Croats, 12 Yugoslav and 17 other origins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the distance from the Hotel Vitez to the village of Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 4.4 kms by road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by car, travelling by car, how much time would it take to get from the Hotel Vitez to Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again using the same conditions as I described earlier, about six minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the village of Santici visible from the main road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Leach, I am going to ask you to return to Exhibit 29C and place that back on the ELMO. Actually let me ask you one other question in respect of Santici. When did the attack take place on Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 16th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you, Mr. Leach, to point out to the court on that exhibit the village of Nadioci. Where, Mr. Leach, is Nadioci in respect to Vitez? How far away is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nadioci is approximately 6 kms from Vitez, from the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can finish with that particular exhibit, Mr. Leach. How many minutes by car is it from the Hotel Vitez to Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under normal driving conditions, seven minutes approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the 1991 census figures in respect of that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population, 474. Bosnian Muslims, 42; Bosnian Serbs, 27; Bosnian Croats, 386; Yugoslavs, 6; other origins 13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, I'm now going to in just a minute ask that there be tape number 7 played for the court. Can you explain to the court in advance what they'll be seeing on video tape number 7?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. In the village of Nadioci a certain number of houses were destroyed, which were adjacent -- between the road and adjacent to the River Lasva. These are often referred to by eye witnesses as weekend houses. They would normally be used by residents throughout the area to have a break during the weekends before the conflict took place and are therefore referred to as weekend houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who resided in those weekend houses in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time refugees, Bosnian Muslim refugees from a variety of locations in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now if we could have the lights lowered, please, and we could play tape number 7. Mr. Leach, if you want to narrate as we go along in this, please feel free to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These pictures were taken with a hand held video camera, again by assistants from the Dutch national police. At the time of the year the vegetation, as you can see, was quite extensive. We are travelling from the direction of the Busovaca T-junction towards the village of Ahmici and Santici, if we were to look at a map or at other exhibits, and the villages are there seen from the road -- sorry -- the houses are seen from the road and the River Lasva is behind the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask now to have the usher present our next exhibit, and I would also ask that that tape, which would be Exhibit 48, be introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. That will be P48.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think that this is Section 7 of the cassette which is numbered 34 and it is 34/4, since the other four were already admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is that all right, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's quite all right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, could you please identify what this exhibit is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is there a difficulty, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is just helpful to know what number has been assigned to the exhibits before the testimony about it commences your Honour. Perhaps we could have a statement when an exhibit is given to the witness that "the witness is being provided with Exhibit 47" or whatever. That would be very helpful to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This should be Exhibit 48; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Then referring to Exhibit 48, Mr. Leach, can you identify what this exhibit represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This represents a series of still photographs of the houses -- a selection of the houses you've just seen portrayed on the video clip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when those photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date of that, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken on Sunday, 26th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these photographs accurately represent the damage and destruction to the weekend houses in Nadioci on that particular date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce Exhibit 48 into evidence. Then, Mr. Leach, if you would be so kind as to put on the ELMO exhibit photograph Z1/932. Would you explain what that particular exhibit represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a representative sample of one of the houses, one of the weekend houses, which was -- is damaged, as portrayed in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you next place on the ELMO Z1/933? Mr. Leach, what does that photograph represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is another photograph of one of the Nadioci weekend houses taken from the road. We didn't go down actually any closer to that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you now turn to Z1/934? Mr. Leach, please describe what that exhibit represents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again this is another photograph of one of the weekend houses alongside the River Lasva and the main road between Vitez and the Busovaca T-junction towards Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Turn to Z1/961, please. Would you explain what that particular photograph represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again another of the weekend houses between the main road, the main highway and the River Lasva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you turn to Z1/962, please? What does that photograph represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's another photograph taken from the main highway of one of the weekend houses in Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lastly, would you turn to Z1/964, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a close-up where we were able to get nearer to the house of one of the weekend houses in Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Leach. I'll give you just a minute to reassemble that exhibit. Mr. Leach, I would now like to turn to the village of Pirici. First of all, can you inform the court when that attack took place on the village of Pirici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was again on 16th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you again return to Exhibit 29C, place that on the ELMO so you can direct the court to the location of Pirici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are holding the pointer now on the village of Pirici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to the census figures in respect of Pirici, Mr. Leach, what were those census figures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population was 225. Bosnian Muslims at 110; Bosnian Serbs, 3; Bosnian Croats, 98; Yugoslavs, 5; and other origins, 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was Pirici from the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is approximately 5 kms to Pirici and that would take approximately eight minutes by car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now ask that another set of photographs be marked as Prosecutor's Exhibit 49. Mr. Leach, can you identify what's contained in Prosecutor's Exhibit 49?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are photographs again, your Honours, taken while I was present by the Dutch National Police. These were taken again on Sunday, 26th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do they accurately represent damage that you observed on that particular date in that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce Prosecutor's Exhibit 49. Now, Mr. Leach, I would like to turn to a number of those photographs. I would like to start with Z1/975 and ask you to place that on the ELMO, please. Would you explain what is depicted in that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pirici is only a small hamlet rather than full village, as it were. This is taken almost in the centre of the main grouping of houses in Pirici. Pirici is on a hill side, which overlooks the main Vitez to Zenica highway. For example, it overlooks the village of Santici. It overlooks the village of Ahmici. If you are stood in Pirici, for example, you can see the lower mosque in Ahmici quite clearly even today. The photograph you have here in the far distance, you can see the town of Vitez itself. You can see a grouping of buildings, which is mainly red and white, in the centre portion of the photograph (indicating). Then as I take the pointer right, you can see what is a chimney stack or a smoke stack. That is a chemical or explosives factory which was situated just outside Vitez in between the villages of Gacice and Veceriska. It is a fairly good representative idea of what you can see from Pirici down into Vitez town and to some extent vice versa if you were stood in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Thank you very much. Would you now turn to Z1/976, please. Would you explain what that depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a photograph of one of the houses in the village of Pirici itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you turn to Z1/977, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Similarly that is another photograph taken on 26th May of one of the houses in Pirici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you turn to Z1/972, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is another photograph of the house. The previous one was, if you will, below the road. If you were going to walk off the main road -- off the road in the village, you would walk downhill. This photograph you now see is on the other side of the road, as if you were walking up the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Turn to photograph Z1/978.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is another photograph quite close-up of one of the houses in Pirici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Leach, would you turn to Z1/981, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again that's another one of the houses in Pirici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lastly, would you turn to Z1/983, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again that's a close-up view of one of the porches of one of the houses in Pirici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Leach. Would you reassemble that exhibit, please? Mr. President, while Mr. Leach is reassembling that particular exhibit, does the court intend to take a break at 11.15? If so, this would be perhaps a good opportunity to break because I have a series of exhibits that come in a logical order next?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Tribunal is very pleased to respond favourably to your request. We will take a break and start again at 11.35. (11.15 am) (Short break) (11.30 am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing can now resume. Please have the accused brought in. (Accused re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I would like the usher to take our next exhibit to Mr. Dubuisson, please. Again, Mr. President, with this particular exhibit there is a photograph for the exhibit, one photograph for your Honours, two photocopies for your Honours and one photocopy for the Defence. Mr. Leach, I would like to refer you now to Exhibit 50 and ask you to describe what that exhibit represents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is another aerial photograph provided to us under Rule 70 by the British Ministry of Defence in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it taken, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph was taken on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce Exhibit 50, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Without waiving any objections we may have to the use of Rule 70, your Honour, we have no objection to this as well as the other aerial photos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I agree with Mr. Hayman. You should explain in a little bit more detail. Let me recall Rule 70, because two maps were introduced. I'm looking at 70B. I suppose that's the rule, Mr. Harmon. For the public I would like to recall -- this is not for the parties or the judges: "If the Prosecutor is in possession of information which has been provided to him on a confidential basis and which has used solely for the purpose of generating new evidence, that initial information and its origins shall not be disclosed by the Prosecutor without the consent of the person or entity providing the initial information and shall in any event not be used or given in evidence without prior disclosure to the accused". We won't get into any discussions about this here, but the Prosecutor has indicated that this is covered by Rule 70, which I suppose is proper. This is a precedent which I suppose would be followed. Therefore, it was a good thing for it to be communicated precisely. So having said that, we can admit this exhibit as exhibit number 50. Go ahead, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right, your Honour. Thank you. Mr. Leach, would you describe what that particular exhibit represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. This is -- if I use the marker, this road I point to now is the main road between Vitez to Zenica. I'll indicate that for you again, your Honours (indicating). Vitez would be in this direction going that way and Zenica and the Busovaca turn-off would be going in that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the photograph you will see certain areas that have been labelled. The area here to the left of centre is the area of Pirici. If I move the pointer directly to the right, you then come to the village of Santici. If one were to follow the road to the next main village you start at the village of Ahmici and then certain buildings that are visible on the aerial photograph are individually labelled. The label being placed to indicate an area which is Lower Ahmici (indicating). There's a label for the mosque with the minaret, which is 2-3 cms just to the right of the label. You can see the minaret is tumbled to one side. To the left of that is the upper mosque in Ahmici. To the left of that is the very end of the village, Upper Ahmici. Also indicated on the aerial photograph for you, your Honours, is the Catholic cemetery, which other witnesses may refer to during their testimony later. Hence it has been labelled for you now. Another location which is referred to as the bungalow, there is no building there. There formerly was. Again other witnesses in their testimony will refer you to this building and hence it has been labelled for you at this stage now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, a few minutes ago you testified about a photograph from the village of Pirici. It was photograph Z1/975, and it showed a view from Pirici back into Vitez. Would you point on that particular map where you were standing when that particular photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was approximately in this area here, your Honours (indicating).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can you say the number again of the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Z1/975 from the photographs relating to Pirici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Where is the river exactly in this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And the weekend area which you mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Judge Riad, that will be on a following photograph. Mr. Leach, you have been to this area many times. You have said that in your previous testimony. Does this particular exhibit, Exhibit 50, accurately depict the area that's shown in the photograph itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Particularly in Ahmici it's very, very much the same as it stands today and as this picture was taken in 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Now if we could have the usher please take the next exhibit? Now, Mr. Leach, referring to Exhibit 51, was that also provided pursuant to Rule 70?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me the date that that picture was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Subject to the potential objections of counsel, your Honour, we would move to introduce Exhibit 51 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Same comment as to the last exhibit, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Perhaps, your Honour -- I have a series of these exhibits that I will be introducing. If the court would note the objection of counsel as to all of these, when I introduce these, we may be able to proceed a little bit faster; in other words, he has a standing objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That's fine. It is not a standing objection, your Honour. It's a reservation of rights to object to the way in which Rule 70 may be sought to be applied to these exhibits, because I do not know exactly in what way the Prosecution may seek to limit my cross-examination concerning these exhibits. So I'm simply reserving my rights in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to supplement something in order to shed some light on the position of the Trial Chamber. This is an observation which the judges also make, in so far as this does not call into question our principle of accepting all exhibits as evidence, but here the Judge can control conditions under which these documents were disclosed by the Prosecutor, and whether this is respecting the condition which says that they can be exhibited -- they can be admitted as exhibits for the judges only if there is consent on the part of the person or the entity having supplied them. Therefore, the Prosecutor has to give proof of that consent. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Mr. President. Mr. Leach, will you proceed to describe that particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the main, your Honours, this is an aerial photograph of the village of Nadioci, which is the main area in the main centre part of the photograph. To ease reference to the previous photograph, we have again labelled, as we did in the first one. So, for example, at the bottom centre is the area of housing which would be Upper Ahmici. To the right of your Honours will see the upper mosque, the one without a minaret. To the right of that, in the bottom right-hand corner, is Lower Ahmici, and one can actually see there as well the lower mosque with the minaret. The Catholic cemetery isn't fully depicted there. The building I referred to earlier as the bungalow is here (indicating). The main road to Zenica goes through the whole photograph. Damaged or destroyed houses, the weekend houses, are in this area here, your Honours. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your Honour, I would like to have another aerial photograph passed up to the Registrar. Mr. Leach, would you please identify Exhibit 52?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As previously, your Honours, it's British Ministry of Defence aerial photograph. The --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it taken, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The main highway from Vitez to the Busovaca turn-off and Zenica is here. Vitez would be in this direction. Busovaca and Zenica would be in that direction. (Indicating). At this point here you see a T-junction, a road junction. This road, which goes through the centre of the photograph, is what you will hear other witnesses refer to as the mountain road. This is a route which goes over the hilly areas, the mountain areas, of this area, central Bosnia, to Zenica. Labelled on the photograph for you is Dubravica School, which also other witnesses will refer to for you, and in the top right-hand corner is an UNPROFOR followed by IFOR or SFOR base or garrison, which is often referred to as Santici Base. That covers the whole of this area which is in white. At the time on 16th April this was manned by soldiers from the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Leach. I would like to turn to our next exhibit. All right. Mr. Leach, could you please, referring to Exhibit 53 -- referring to Exhibit 53, Mr. Leach, can you describe the source of that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again this is from the British Ministry of Defence, then provided under Rule 70, and again taken on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We would move to introduce this photograph into evidence, your Honour. Now, Mr. Leach, please describe for the Trial Chamber and for counsel what this photograph represents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph is basically a summary or a blow-up of the three previous photographs you've seen, which gives an indication of the distances and how the three photographs, if we were to lay those out on a large table, you could actually join these three previous photographs together. This photograph does that for to you. Again I will point to certain locations which have been indicated. The Dubravica School. Just above the Dubravica School is the mountain road I referred to in the last photograph. Thereafter there is Santici Base, which was with the Netherlands soldiers there in 1993. The village of Santici is the area above the label, marked "Santici". (Indicating) the village of Pirici is to the left on the hill top. Below Pirici but above on the photograph, of course, is Ahmici. Again the Catholic cemetery (indicating), the location of the bungalow and the weekend houses in between the main highway and the River Lasva at the top of the photograph in the centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. Where is the Vitez Hotel in this big map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This isn't shown on this photograph, your Honour, but if a similar photograph of a similar scale was shown, I would estimate it would be ... (indicating).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It would be higher or lower than other villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The high ground is this area here, your Honour (indicating). The low ground and the river valley, if you will, by the main road is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And the Vitez Hotel is on high ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the Vitez Hotel is on low ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Low ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Dubuisson, has Exhibit 52 been entered into evidence? No. Then I would move Exhibit 52 into evidence and this evidence as well. Now, Mr. Leach, we are going to see a video tape. It is video tape number 1. Before it's shown to the Trial Chamber and to counsel, can you explain what will be seen on that particular video tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We were in a helicopter provided by IFOR. The beginning of the clip will show from approximately this area with the photographs or the video taking shots in that direction (indicating). The helicopter then flew traversing the main highway and into Vitez town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the lights could be dimmed, please, so we could play tape number 1? (Video tape played)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the area of Lower Ahmici and the helicopter is circling around here (indicating). You can see the road into Ahmici in the centre of the photograph and the Ahmici mosque. We are now south of the main highway, travelling in an east to west direction, as indicated on the picture. The main road is approximately in the centre, just above centre, of this picture that you can see in front of you. The area coming into view now from the left of the screen is the Santici Base, which is very much now as it was then in 1993. You can see traffic moving on the main highway. Just coming into picture was the junction which would be the mountain road, which is centre, just above centre now. Dubravica School is just out of shot. You can't quite clearly see it now. The main road into Vitez is below us now, with traffic travelling down it, where the freeze frame is held. If you were on the main highway you would turn left and travel down the road towards the bottom of the screen. That would take you into Vitez town and towards Hotel Vitez itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that that particular clip be introduced into evidence. I would like you to turn to the village of Donja Veceriska and I would ask you to place a small concentric circle map, which I believe is 29C, on to the ELMO. Could you point out the village of Donja Veceriska on that particular map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Leach. This was the village of Donja Veceriska attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on 16th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you provide to the court and counsel the 1991 census figures for that particular village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total number of inhabitants at the time from the 1991 census is 710. Bosnian Muslims were 388. Bosnian Serbs, 3. Bosnian Croats, 306. 8 Yugoslav and 5 of other origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now from the Hotel Vitez how far away is the village of Donja Veceriska located, that is by road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By road it's approximately 3.9 km, which can take approximately six minutes to drive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now does the village of Donja Veceriska sit next to a factory of some sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It sits next to a large complex chemical works and what was used to produce explosives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That will lead me, Mr. Leach, into the next video clip, which is film clip number 9. Before we show that, would you explain to the court and to counsel what will be depicted on tape number 9?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the town plan and the Vitez aerial photograph that you were shown earlier, you saw the area of Stari Vitez. This is again a video taken from the air in an IFOR helicopter. It mainly covers the distance and a view of travelling from Stari Vitez to the chemical plant with the villages of Gacice and Veceriska either side of the plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we lower the lights, please and show tape number 9? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the area of Stari Vitez. Just leaving right of shot was the area where there was a large grave site. This is a patch of open ground, very flat. The chemical plant is now coming into view. It's a series of buildings. The main centre point to note for the location is the smoke stack. The village of Veceriska was to the right and again this is a view of the chemical plant. The village of Gacice comes into view in the centre picture now from the left. So the villages of Gacice and Veceriska are either side of the chemical plant. That is Veceriska there and you can see the houses without roofs. Then a series of other houses that are destroyed and some that are not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would move to introduce that film into evidence as the Prosecutor's exhibit. My next exhibit, your Honour, I have a photo album I would like to present. Mr. Leach, you have before you Exhibit 54?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please identify what that exhibit contains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a selection of photographs. The very first photograph, PH338, is taken from Stari Vitez close to where the front line was, looking towards the smoke stack for the chemical factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you go into the actual description, this a series of photographs? Were you present when those photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was. The remaining photographs out of this bundle are a selection of photographs taken actually in the village of Veceriska itself, and they were taken on Tuesday, 28th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would move to introduce Exhibit 54 as Prosecutor's exhibit, your Honour. Mr. Leach, referring to a series of those photographs, would you first place on the ELMO photograph P338? Would you describe what that photograph represents, please? Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, you've placed photograph P338 on the ELMO. Would you please describe to the court and to counsel what's depicted in that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When this photograph was taken, we were stood near a series of concrete block garages, which was one of the areas of a front line which developed after the attacks in Stari Vitez and Vitez on 16th April 1993. Although it is not in the picture, beyond those garages would be a running track, which you'll note when you look at other exhibits such as the town plan and aerial photographs. To the right, almost centre picture, but to the right, you can quite clearly see the smoke stack for the chemical plant. To the right of the smoke stack -- unfortunately it's obliterated by a bush, but that's generally the location of where the village of Veceriska would be. To the left of the smoke stack, there is a hilly area and that would be where the village of Gacice would be. The Hotel Vitez would be to the left of the photograph, following the direction of the pointer, that way (indicating), would be almost approximately line of sight to Hotel Vitez if you were to go left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Leach, would you now put on the ELMO Z2/398? Please explain what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was taken when we were in the village itself. What you can see to the left is quite clearly the chemical factory, smoke stack, the red and white chimney. Then in the centre ground opposite, where I'm moving the pointer now (indicating) is the village of Gacice. Below the village and in the lower ground, but with the foliage around it, you can see some of the roofs of the buildings which form part of the chemical plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Leach. Would you turn to photograph Z2/394? What does that photograph show?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That represents a photograph of what you would see or what we saw in 1996 in Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you turn to photograph Z2/372? Would you describe to the Trial Chamber and to counsel what is depicted in that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again this is a selection and one of the houses that you can see in Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lastly, would you turn to Z2/383? What is depicted in that particular photograph, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The centre building is again another one that is damaged and uninhabitable at the moment in Veceriska, or as it was in 1996, I should say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You can reassemble the exhibit, Mr. Leach. If the usher could please introduce -- take the next exhibit. Mr. Leach, referring to Prosecutor's Exhibit 55, can you describe the source of that exhibit and the date it was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once again, your Honour, this is provided by the British Ministry of Defence, provided to us under Rule 70. It was taken on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce this particular photograph into evidence as the Prosecutor's next exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, would you please Orient all of us to what this particular exhibit represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a photograph of the village of Donia Veceriska in the centre ground with the Vitez chemical plant above it (indicating). The village of Gacice would be across the valley. I should say Veceriska is on high ground. The chemical plant is on low ground in a small valley. Gacice would be in this area again on high ground. The town of Vitez would be in this direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, there's a sticker that says "the Vitez chemical plant". Underneath that particular sticker there appears to be some smoke coming up. Can you explain what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is smoke that's coming out of the smoke stack. Obviously you can quite clearly see that the smoke is visible to the human eye and would be for a considerable distance around the area. So, for example, if you were stood in Vitez and were looking to that area, Gacice, the chemical plant and Donia Veceriska, you could see smoke whether it was coming from the chemical plant or from any other building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Leach. Now I would like to turn, Mr. Leach, if I could, to the village of Loncari and ask you, first of all, when was that village attacked by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was attacked on 16th and 17th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you kindly put Exhibit 29C back on the ELMO, that is the small map with the concentric circles, and identify for the Trial Chamber the location of that particular village? Your Honour, I apologise. I need one more exhibit in the last series of exhibits for you. It's out of order. So if I could introduce one more exhibit before we come back to ... We will come back to the village of Loncari in just a minute, your Honour. Mr. Leach, you have before you Prosecutor's Exhibit 56. Was this also provided by the British government pursuant to Rule 70?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date that this particular exhibit was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce Prosecutor's Exhibit 56 into evidence. Mr. Leach, please explain what this particular photograph represents, using the legend that's attached to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the -- this is another, much smaller scale but representative photograph of the area of Vitez itself. If I go -- going through the legend, number A (indicating) is the Hotel Vitez. B is the cinema building and the headquarters of Mario Cerkez. C is the PTT building. D, the Chess Club. E, the approximate location of the front line as it developed on 16th April. F is the mosque in Stari Vitez. G is the site where the bodies are buried in a large grave site in Stari Vitez. H is the ABiH, the Armija, headquarters in Stari Vitez. I is the location of the veterinary station, which witnesses will talk about during their testimony. J is the Dubravica School. Although not labelled, above J you can see the Santici Base. Sorry. That should be K. Sorry, no. It's not labelled, your Honours. K is this location down here (indicating). K is what was known as the British Battalion Echelon Garage, as I referred to in earlier testimony. This is where the UNPROFOR vehicles from Landrovers right through to Armoured Personnel Carriers, etc., would refuel and would go for refitting, engine repairs, etc. Witnesses will refer to this location in their testimony. L is the chemical plant. As from the previous photograph, you can see the same smoke on a small scale. M is the village of Gacice on the high ground above the chemical plant. N is the village of Donia Veceriska on the high ground on the opposite side of the valley from Gacice, above the chemical plant. O is over back into Vitez, Stari Vitez, the approximate location where the truck bomb exploded on 19th April 1993. P is the approximate location of where the opposite side of the Stari Vitez front line would be (indicating). Again I should perhaps refer you to this small road here above the Dubravica School. That would be the mountain road to Zenica, at this junction here, and on the exhibits from the air, where we flee from Ahmici into Vitez and I pointed out vehicles driving into Vitez town, having turned off the main highway, that is this road here. So you would drive down off the main highway into Vitez, past I, the veterinary station, along into Vitez itself, and get to the Hotel Vitez in the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Leach. Now, Mr. Leach, I would like to return to the village of Loncari. You pointed out that village previously. Can you please provide to the court and to counsel the 1991 census figures for that particular village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Loncari, the total population, 1991, was 314. Of those, 249 were Bosnian Muslim, 249. 20 Serb; 44 Bosnian Croat; and 1 Yugoslav. No others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, your Honour. I would like to now introduce for identification another large aerial image. Mr. Leach, was that photograph provided pursuant to Rule 70 by the British government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date that this particular photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again I think this is on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We would move to introduce this photograph into evidence, your Honour. Mr. Leach, can you proceed to describe the salient locations on that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. The central location, which is indicated with a label, is the village of Loncari. The other salient features of this photograph is the main highway as it continues off from the previous photographs. So, for example, the route to Vitez (indicating) would be that way. A short journey down here would take you to the Nadioci weekend houses, the bungalow, the cemetery, etc., and on towards Vitez. The highway continues and that would be the main highway across the top of the photograph, to Zenica. Indicated here is the location I've referred to several times as the Busovaca T-junction. So if one were travelling from Vitez to Busovaca, one would turn right here, and that would lead you down into the town and municipality of Busovaca. Although there's only one or two buildings, maybe three depicted, you can see three stripes, which are roofs of buildings in a location known as Kaonik camp. Other witnesses will refer to this location, your Honours: this was a former JNA barracks, which was later under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, were you able to enter the village of Loncari and take photographs of the buildings that were damaged or destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. During the time we took photographs, the various stills you have seen of villages that were damaged, we were escorted by IFOR. That escort included engineers from the Royal Engineers of the British army, who were there to indicate to us where mine fields were present. As a result of their concerns about the safety of travelling on foot and on the roads as well, the hard road surface in that area as well, we were not allowed to enter Loncari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to turn to our next exhibit, which is another large aerial image. Mr. Leach, you have before you Prosecutor's exhibit number 58. I think we can move through this exhibit particularly quickly. If you would just describe, first of all, was this photograph provided by the British military as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was again pursuant to Rule 70, and again taken on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you kindly describe to the court and to counsel the salient features that are depicted in this particular image?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This location here, your Honours, labelled is the Busovaca T-junction, which you saw on the previous photograph with the road to Zenica going ahead (indicating). One would turn right here to travel into the town of Busovaca along this road. The road into the village of Loncari is here. You have the whole view, aerial view of the area known as Kaonik camp here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Leach. I'll now turn to another large aerial image. I would ask that Exhibit 58 be moved into evidence, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: D' accord.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, turning your attention to Prosecutor's Exhibit 59, was this also provided by the British government pursuant to Rule 70?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date this particular photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again on or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce Prosecutor's Exhibit 59 into evidence. Mr. Leach, will you please describe the salient features depicted in Prosecutor's Exhibit 59?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the village of Ahmici can be seen in the bottom right-hand corner. That is Upper Ahmici and the upper mosque can be seen in that area. Above that is the location of the bungalow. Following the main Vitez to Zenica highway, the weekend houses at Nadioci. As one would continue along the highway, if one was to take a left turn, that would lead you to the village of Loncari, which is almost centre picture, just below centre. Going back to the junction and continuing adjacent to the junction, the V of the junction is Kaonik camp. Busovaca T-junction, the road to Zenica. From the Busovaca T-junction, one could follow the road and in the top right-hand corner one could see the initial part of the town of Busovaca itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Leach. Now I turn to my next exhibit, Mr. Leach, which is an album of photographs. Mr. Leach, you have had placed before you Prosecutor's exhibit number 60. Can you please, first of all, identify whether you were present when those photographs were taken and when they were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was present when these photographs were taken. They were taken in the town of Busovaca on Saturday, 25th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do they accurately depict the destruction of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Leach, can you tell me where that particular mosque is located in the town of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's in what I would describe as the centre of the town, the town centre, adjacent to shopping areas, close to a bus station, close to a market area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please remove the first of those photographs, Z1/869, and place it on the ELMO and describe to the court and to counsel what that particular photograph represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a picture of the mosque from the path leading to the front of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now would you please place on the ELMO Z1/878? What does that show, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again a mosque from the right-hand side of the building from the front door. Where the pointer is showing (indicating) now would be the base of the minaret. One can see where the minaret has tumbled towards the photographer, if I should say, and the top of the minaret with its small veranda and small handrail is in the centre of the bottom right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, would you now place the next photograph, which is Z1/874, on the ELMO? What does that show, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the inside of the mosque, the roof struts in this area at the top of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Leach. Your Honour, I would move to introduce Prosecutor's Exhibit 60 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, how many more exhibits of this type do you have to show?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Photographs, your Honour, large photographs? I haven't counted them but I have a number of them, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What I suggest, together with my colleagues, is that we will break now and that for technical reasons the room will not be available until 3 o'clock this afternoon, but we will sit until 6 o'clock. I'm now suspending the hearing. (12.45 pm) (Luncheon adjournment) 21 22 23 24 25 (3.00 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please have the accused brought in. (Accused re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, if I'm not mistaken, we were at Exhibit 61.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We are now about to go to Exhibit 61, Mr. President. Now, Mr. Leach, can you please identify what Prosecutor's Exhibit 61 is and the source of that particular map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. This is a town plan of the town of Kiseljak in Kiseljak Municipality, central Bosnia. It's produced by the Director General of the Military Survey, Ministry of Defence, United Kingdom and was printed in May 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please put that on the ELMO? I would like you to point out in that exhibit, Mr. Leach, the location of the Kiseljak Military Barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The Kiseljak Military Barracks are this group of buildings here. It's actually indicated on the map. It actually says "Kiseljak Military Barracks".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Leach, what is the significance of that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was an HVO headquarters and was one of the headquarters of General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, would you now turn to Exhibit 29D and put that on the ELMO? 29D is a part of a larger exhibit 29 that has a series of concentric circles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the centre point of the first circle is the Kiseljak Military Barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
