utterances.text: That's correct, your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Leach. That's enough with that exhibit. Now we are going to turn, Mr. Leach, to tape number 4. If you would kindly explain to the court and to counsel what will be seen on tape number 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a very short video clipping again of an aerial over flight from a helicopter, using an IFOR helicopter, where you can see the Kiseljak Barracks from the air. This was taken in May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we dim the lights, please, and roll tape number 4? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the barracks before you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce both exhibit number 61, the map, and the tape number 4 as Prosecutor's next exhibit in order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The document and the tape will be put into the record. Has this been numbered?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. It's 34 -- it will be numbered as 34/7.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, now we are going to turn to another tape. It's tape number 22. Can you please explain to the Chamber and counsel what will be seen on tape number 22?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Similar to the previous tape, your Honours, this is again taken from a helicopter with the assistance of the Dutch police and is an over flight and aerial view of a damaged mosque just close to the centre of Kiseljak, on the way into Kiseljak from the direction of Busovaca. So it's north of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the tape done, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was done again in May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we dim the lights and roll tape number 22? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The mosque is the building upper centre ground. You can just see the remains of the dome area. It's now gone out of picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. That was a little quick. I know that Mr. Leach is very familiar with this, but I think I can speak for my colleagues and say perhaps you could either slow it down a little bit and show us where it is. Can we see it again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I appreciate that, your Honour, and I will ask to roll tape number 22 again please. If there's any way to slow it down from the room upstairs, I would appreciate that being done as well. (Video tape replayed)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The mosque is the building, your Honours, which is just coming in from the left of the picture. It's now centre picture, perhaps two-thirds of the way up the screen. The main highway into Kiseljak from north to south is in front of the mosque. It's actually on the highway as you drive into Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that that be introduced as Prosecutor's Exhibit 34/7.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think it is part of another tape which has not yet been introduced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This was 22 according to the Prosecutor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, it was a section of a tape. I think its number should be 62, so that this would be 62/1, having to do with the section 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is that all right? Has the Defence noted that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a photo album, which would be my next exhibit. Mr. Leach, turning to Exhibit 63, can you identify that photo album?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can, your Honours. This is a selection of photographs of the mosque on the north side of the town of Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Thursday, 23rd May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when they were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do those photographs accurately depict the damage as shown in those particular photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce Prosecutor's Exhibit 63. Mr. Leach, would you take the first photograph, Z1/639, place it on the ELMO and explain to the court what that particular photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a side view of the mosque. As you saw in the previous picture of the mosque in Busovaca, the minaret has fallen over by whatever means and is lying in front of the mosque on its side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Would you turn to the next photograph, which is Z1/638, place that on the ELMO and explain to the Trial Chamber and counsel what is seen in that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you stand at the main entrance into the mosque that is the view you would have of the burnt-out damage and the destruction inside the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now turning, Mr. Leach, to Z1/650, would you repeat what you just did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The previous photograph you could see an archway when you were stood in the entrance. If you then stood at the archway in the mosque, that is then what you would see inside the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Will you reassemble the exhibit, please? Mr. Leach, we are going to turn to the village of Gomionica. Let me ask you first, when was the date the HVO attacked the village of Gomionica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on 18th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn to Exhibit 29D, place that on the ELMO and point out where the village of Gomionica is in relation to the town of Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just hold your pointer there for a minute. All right, Mr. Leach. Can you tell us, referring to the 1991 census figures, what the census figures report in respect of the village of Gomionica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population, your Honours, was 427. Of those, Bosnian Muslims were 417; Bosnian Croats, 6; and 4 other origins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Leach, what is the distance from the Kiseljak Barracks to the village of Gomionica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's 6.6 kms, which under normal driving conditions would take approximately nine minutes to drive to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been to the village, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you saw when you were at the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's very similar to what you have seen depicted in Ahmici. The whole village or the portion of it off the main road is destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are going to turn to a video tape. It's tape number 15. Again can you please orient the court and counsel what will be seen on that particular video tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. On this video tape you will see Gomionica and another location just to the north of it called Behrici from the air again taken from an IFOR helicopter. For the purposes of your record, your Honours, all the aerial photography that is being shown to you was taken on Monday, 27th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please could we dim the lights and roll tape 13? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the village, your Honours, coming from north of the village. This is an adjacent village which you will see on later exhibits called Behrici. The helicopter here is circling round in order to try to encompass as many of the buildings as possible in the shots. This is the southern part of the village of Gomionica. In effect at this stage, your Honours, we are heading towards the main highway, the Kiseljak to Busovaca highway and traversing the highway. At this point the highway would be below you, if you were in the helicopter, and the buildings now in view is lower Gomionica. Now travelling along the highway in the direction of Busovaca. Damaged buildings are evident in the foreground and now in the centre ground. That is the main area of Gomionica itself. The village does extend up into the hillside, again very similar in style to Ahmici. It's spread over some distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce that film clip as Prosecutor's exhibit 62/2. No?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. That will be section 13, which means it's 34/8.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: 34/8. Then I am going to defer to Mr. Dubuisson to indicate appropriately which exhibit number is attached to it, because I am not succeeding. Mr. Leach, we are going to turn now to tape 14 section of video tape. I will leave it to Mr. Dubuisson to mark it with the appropriate number and inform counsel of what that number is. Before we get there, Mr. Leach, can you explain to the court and to counsel what they will see in this particular section of tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The process of this is that the Dutch photographer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: May I just ask a question without interrupting you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mentioned that the population of Gomionica was 427, 417 Muslims and 6 Croats. Which date was that? Was it when you went there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The village is completely destroyed, uninhabited at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Uninhabited now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So nobody is left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Loncari was 249 Muslim, 20 Serbs and 40 Croats. Is this the census now or before the destruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the census in 1991. As regards the village of Loncari, your Honours, it is my understanding that Bosnian Muslims are attempting to move back into the village and rebuild their homes, so there may well be some Bosnian Muslim residents in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Describe to Trial Chamber and counsel what we will see in tape section 14.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is taken from a vehicle that moved through the village of Gomionica, again similar to the one you saw when I testified two weeks ago, starting from the top of the village, and the video was placed on a vehicle and we drove down through the village trying to view as much of the scene on the ground as we possibly could, subject to foliage and what have you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we lower the lights and roll tape 14? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At this stage, your Honours, we have actually started -- I was incorrect before -- we have started at the bottom of the village. The vehicle now probably 150 metres from the main highway between Kiseljak and Busovaca. In order to try to keep the camera as steady as possible, again, as in Ahmici, we went quite slow. We're now entering what would be the main area of the village. There are houses either side of this road all in a very similar condition to as you see now. The turn-off that we've just seen would be a right-hand turn, where you would drive down that road to reach what I would describe as lower Gomionica, which you saw in the previous aerial video. Gomionica is a village, your Honours, which again is split up. There is a lower part, a main or middle part of the village, and then as one drives further on, there's a gap without any housing and then you get to the top of the village and you have the upper part of the village. We are' still in what I would best describe as middle Gomionica at the moment. At that point where you could see a distinct break in the film, that's where a portion has been edited out because there's nothing to see. There's a break in the village. We've now reached the upper part of the village. I would say that the break in housing is 350-450 metres. I haven't measured it, but it's about that distance. The road at this area of the village, it's on a very elevated portion. The main part of the village is below, to the right, and then lower Gomionica is nearer towards Kiseljak. It is more of a dirt track than a tarmacadam or an asphalt road at this stage. It was very difficult to try and encapsulate everything in a video without taking a video travelling up through the village and then unfortunately having to repeat the process driving back down. I think you can see, your Honours, in some of the houses where there's only walls left and there's no roof that there's a substantial amount of foliage and even to some extent trees have even grown over the last two to three years. Again the break in the video there was where we left the upper part of the village and we are now coming back into middle Gomionica. The main highway between Kiseljak and Busovaca would be down below the village now in the valley floor. This is still in the main part or what I would call middle Gomionica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce that portion of the film as the Prosecutor's next exhibit, 34/9?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, is that correct.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it's 34/9.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, we are now going to move to another portion of a video, it's tape number 15. Can you please explain to the court and counsel what they'll see in that particular film clip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I indicated earlier that there was a right-hand turn near the main highway at the bottom of the village, where you would drive into lower Gomionica. The clipping you'll see now is again video footage taken from a vehicle in the lower part of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could we dim the lights, please, and play that portion of the film? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this occasion, your Honours, we have started at what is the end of the road into lower Gomionica. The main part of the village is currently behind the cameraman. Kiseljak would be in the direction that the camera is pointing now. Unlike Vitez, it would be difficult to have line of sight from Kiseljak to this area. The main highway would be in the direction that the cameraman is now facing. We are now leaving the end of lower Gomionica and driving back towards the middle part of the village. At this point the vehicle turns right and is now travelling directly towards the middle part of the village and this road runs parallel almost with the main highway. So, in effect, you are travelling in the direction from Kiseljak towards Busovaca. In this area you can see that not all the houses are damaged in the lower part of Gomionica and people are living there at this moment in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Is anybody living there now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the lower part of Gomionica yes, there are some residents in maybe 15 to 20 houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: They came back or they --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand that they are of Bosnian Croat ethnicity, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to introduce that portion of the film as Prosecutor's exhibit 34/10. As my next exhibit, your Honour, I have a photograph, which I would like to tender to the court. I would ask that it be marked exhibit number 64. Mr. Leach, referring to Prosecutor's exhibit number 64, would you please place that photograph on the ELMO? Let me ask you, before you comment on it, were you there when that particular photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was taken on Friday, 24th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that accurately portray sections of the village of Gomionica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to explain to the court and counsel what is depicted in that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What we noticed when we were travelling round the area is that, as with many of the highways in central Bosnia, they go through the valley floor. We were on the opposite side of the valley on a hill top, not a very high one, a small hill, and looking across the main road and then looking into the distance, one could see Gomionica in the distance. The photographer then took a photograph, albeit with a telephoto lens, but quite clearly one can from the other side of the main road on a hill top, that is what you would see of Gomionica. The actual road that you see in the picture, if I indicate with the pointer (indicating) is the road that the photographs you have just seen from the video clipping, as you drive up and down that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that photograph number 64 be admitted as the Prosecutor's next exhibit. Mr. Leach, I would now like to turn to the village of Behrici. First I would like to ask you when did the HVO attack the village of Behrici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behrici was attacked on 18th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you start by taking Exhibit 29D, placing it on will ELMO and indicating to the court and counsel the location of the village of Behrici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are pointing to an area right up at the 5 km concentric ring; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The village is to the left of the highlighted name. As you saw on the aerial clipping earlier, Behrici and Gomionica are very close together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the distance from the Kiseljak Barracks to the village of Behrici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 6.5 kms, which would take approximately seven minutes under normal conditions by car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been to the village of Behrici, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About three or four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to the court and counsel the extent of the damage that you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's nothing left. They just destroyed houses. There is nobody living there. Although you are able to walk into it, this is, I understand, still an area where one has to be wary of mines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to the 1991 census figures, Mr. Leach, can you tell us what the 1991 census figures were for the village of Behrici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population, 1991, was 199. Of those, 153 were Bosnian Muslims, 45, Bosnian Croats, and one of other origins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, I'm now going to direct your attention to a video tape. It will be tape Section 16. Before we play that, you could you explain to the court and counsel what they'll see on this particular film clip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a brief aerial clipping, again taken from the IFOR helicopter, on 26th May of Behrici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can we have the lights lowered, please, and play that particular tape? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The helicopter just traverses around the village. You saw some of it earlier in the previous aerial photograph -- aerial video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that that particular section of video tape, a very small section, be introduced as Prosecutor's exhibit 34/11. As my next exhibit, your Honour, I have another photo album, which I would ask be marked as Prosecutor's Exhibit 65. Mr. Leach, let me begin by asking you: were you present when these photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were these photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Friday, 24th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these photographs accurately depict the destruction of buildings that are represented in each photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the Prosecutor's Exhibit 65 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I assume they are photographs of a relevant location. I don't think that has been established yet, what they are -- if this is within the realm of the indictment, we have no objection, but that has not been stated yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I am happy to ask that question, your Honour. Mr. Leach, if I omitted it, where are these photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These photographs are taken actually as you walk in and around the village of Behrici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, would you take photograph Z1/734, place it on the ELMO and please describe to the court and counsel what that photograph represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is an example of the destruction to the houses in Behrici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now refer to photograph Z1/740? Again what does that photograph, Mr. Leach, represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again that's another representative of the housing as it stands or as it stood in 1996 in Behrici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you next turn to photograph Z1/739? Again, Mr. Leach, please explain that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, your Honours, that's as you are in the middle of this village or perhaps it should be referred to as a hamlet. That is what you see in that location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now turn to photograph Z1/730, Mr. Leach, and place that on the ELMO? Again would you describe what that photograph represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again further example of damage in Behrici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn to photograph Z1/728?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, this is another representative sample of the damage in Behrici. I think what this may assist your Honours with is the fact that Behrici is in an elevated location above the main road, and you can see that the valley through to Busovaca, or if one was looking the other way to Kiseljak, in the distance. To Behrici is on a hill side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lastly, Mr. Leach, could you turn to photograph Z1/719, place that on the ELMO and explain to the court what that photograph represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, your Honours, that's another example of how Behrici was in 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll give you a moment to reassemble the exhibit, Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, how far is Behrici away from the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If one was actually to drive from Vitez to Behrici, that would be 34.8 kms, which would take 34, 35 minutes by car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And it's on a higher level than Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is in a completely different municipality from Vitez. This is near Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But it was 6 kms from the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's from Kiseljak Barracks, your Honour, not the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Who was in Kiseljak Barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The HVO was in complete control of Kiseljak Barracks, and it was also a headquarters used by General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Allez-y.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would now like to turn your attention to Svinjarevo. Let me ask you when did the HVO attack the village of Svinjarevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was also on 18th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you refer again to prosecutors Exhibit 29D, place that on the ELMO and indicate with your pointer where the village of Svinjarevo is located in relation to the Kiseljak Barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Leach. What were the census figures in 1991 for the village of Svinjarevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1991, your Honours, the total population was 294. Bosnian Muslims comprised of 282. There was one Yugoslav and 11 of other ethnic origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away was the village of Svinjarevo from the Kiseljak Barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 7.3 kms, which would take 8, 9 minutes by car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you personally been to the village of Svinjarevo, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five or six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the condition of the village of Svinjarevo when you visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not inhabited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the condition of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The buildings are destroyed, as you have seen in other photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, I'm going to ask you to describe two clips, video tapes 17 and 18. I'm going to ask you please to describe what we'll be seeing in those particular clips?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first clip is again one taken from the air in a helicopter. The second clip is one taken from the ground, but this time not driving through the village but just stood statically and panning across the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could the lights be dimmed, please, and could we start with video tape 17? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Basically the helicopter at this moment in time is travelling above the highway between Busovaca and Kiseljak. The helicopter has now turned left away from the highway, is moving away from the highway and into the elevated areas and the hillside where the village is situated. Again the helicopter is now circling as it reaches the highest point of the hill. The village is in the centre ground and the highway would be at the top of the picture. Coming into the frame, almost in the centre ground now is a mosque in Svinjarevo. The helicopter is completing its circle and is now heading back towards the highway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that tape Section 17 be introduced as Prosecutor's exhibit 34/12, and if we could keep the lights dim, we could proceed with video tape section 18. (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, please explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is just where the cameraman is stood upright and he's just holding the camera and he's very slowly traversing around. This is in the upper part of the village. Again you can see it's in an elevated position, the valley down below. The main highway would be in the far distance. We're now presently at the top part of the village. This is the mosque, which is in the upper part of the village. The cameraman has now moved further down. We have probably walked 100, 150 metres further down the village back towards the main road and once again he has just traversed from a static position in the village. Similarly we have moved on again to a separate part of the village. As you can see, your Honours, the damage is fairly consistent as you move from the top of the village, the upper part of the village, down towards the main highway. It's just the same throughout. At this point we are in the very lower part of the village. That's fairly brief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would request that tape clip 18 be admitted as Prosecutor's Exhibit 34/13. As my next exhibit, your Honour, I have a photo album, which I would tender as Prosecutor's exhibit number 66: Mr. Leach, can you describe what Prosecutor's exhibit number 66 is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a sample of photographs that were taken in May 1996, again with the assistance of the Dutch National Police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what location was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was again Svinjarevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when those photographs were taken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do those photographs accurately depict the damage seen in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that Prosecutor's Exhibit 66 be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is 66, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, would you kindly place photograph Z1/771 on the ELMO and explain to the court and counsel what is depicted in that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the mosque which you saw from both the aerial video and from the video on the ground. This is a close-up still from about 20-30 feet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn to photograph Z1/772, please, place that on the ELMO and explain to the court what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a photograph of the inside of the mosque at Svinjarevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lastly, Mr. Leach, could you place on the ELMO photograph Z1/775? Please explain what's depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you go inside the mosque and walk up to a first floor balcony and take a photograph down, that is the sight you see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Leach. Would you reassemble that exhibit, and then we'll turn our attention elsewhere? Mr. Leach, I would like to turn your attention to the village of Gromiljak. Let me begin by asking when did the HVO attack the village of Gromiljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on 18th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you kindly place Exhibit 29D on the ELMO and point out to the court and counsel where the village of Gromiljak is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are indicating it is a little bit to the left of the 4 km mark on Exhibit 29D; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Gromiljak itself is actually either side of the main highway between Kiseljak and Busovaca, north of Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, what do the 1991 census figures show in respect of the village of Gromiljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population for 1991 was 606. Of those, 143 were Bosnian Muslim; 8, Serb; 425, Bosnian Croat; 16, Yugoslav; and 14 of other origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is the village of Gromiljak from Kiseljak Barracks, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's approximately 5.3 kms, which would take approximately five minutes to drive under normal driving conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you personally been to that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the condition of that village, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is mainly intact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now let me ask you, Mr. Leach -- first of all, let me pass up the Prosecutor's next exhibit, which we would tender as Prosecutor's Exhibit 67: now, Mr. Leach, referring to Prosecutor's Exhibit 67, were you present when these photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on Friday, 24th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these photographs taken in the village of Gromiljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is taken on the highway. The photographs you will see is just off the highway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the court and counsel what is depicted just generally in these three photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's three photographs of the mosque in Gromiljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you start, please, by taking photograph Z1/693 and placing that on the ELMO? Please begin your description, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a photograph of the mosque the Gromiljak. The mosque is actually on the highway as you drive past. It's to your left if you are driving towards Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you turn, please, to photograph Z1/698? What does that photograph depict, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the inside of the mosque at Gromiljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lastly, would you turn to photograph Z1/71?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the outside of the mosque at Gromiljak. Similar to those that you may have seen earlier, the minaret has fallen from the outside and fallen across the outside of the gardened area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point out in that particular photograph where the minaret once stood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are pointing to the middle portion of that building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would kindly reassemble that Prosecutor's Exhibit 67, and, your Honours, I would request that Prosecutor's Exhibit 67 be admitted into evidence. Mr. Leach, now you have been in this area many times, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there some Catholic churches in and around this area that you have been testifying about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those Catholic churches destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they still intact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Catholic churches are there? Any recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three, four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, I would like to turn your attention to another location, which is the village of Hercezi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, please, Mr. Leach, first of all, could you take Exhibit 29D, place that on the ELMO and indicate to the court and counsel the location of that particular village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Harmon. I only ask. Was only the mosque in Gromiljak destroyed or other houses destroyed too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From memory, your Honour, there is another house adjacent to the mosque in Gromiljak destroyed. The remainder of the village is still inhabited. There are cafes. There is a church almost opposite, a new church, a factory building nearby. The houses are occupied, I understand, by Bosnian Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, what do the 1991 census figures show in respect of the village of Hercezi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population in Hercezi was 182. 140 were Bosnian Muslim; 42 Bosnian Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, what is the time and the distance from the Kiseljak Barracks to the village of Hercezi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have that information. It's probably in the region of about 7 kms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we are going to be going to video tape number 19. Could you please explain to the court and counsel what will be seen on video tape 19?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a clipping of two sections of video one again is taken from the air in May 1996. The other is taken from the ground, from a static position, stood adjacent to the mosque at Hercezi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, and counsel, this video tape is approximately one minute long. Could we dim the lights, please, and play tape number 19? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The mosque is in the upper left-hand portion of the screen at the moment, right in the corner. The helicopter is circling round. The mosque is now moving into better view. It is now almost in centre picture. That was the aerial view. This is what you see from the ground. The first building, the one in the main picture in the foreground, is the mosque. The building adjacent to that appeared to be some kind of residence for the Imam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that tape number 19 be admitted as Prosecutor's Exhibit 62/2. As my next exhibit, your Honour, I would tender as Prosecutor's Exhibit 68 a photo album. Mr. Leach, let me begin by asking you, are these photographs that were taken in the village of Hercezi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Friday, 24th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these photographs accurately depict the damage that's shown of this particular building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, I would ask that Prosecutor's Exhibit 68 be admitted into evidence. Please, Mr. Leach, would you just put those photographs on the ELMO, starting with Z1/689, and explain to court and counsel what's depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a still photograph of what you have seen from the video footage. The mosque is the left-hand building and what appeared to be a residence was a right-hand building, the residence being the one with the white car near to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, would you now place photograph Z1/690 on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please explain what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the picture from the side of the bidding. The residence is behind this. This is the mosque with the graveyard in the foreground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lastly, would you please place photograph Z1/779 on the ELMO and explain to counsel and the court what is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the inside of the mosque at Hercezi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Leach. Now I'm going to turn your attention to a large aerial photograph, which we would tender as Prosecutor's exhibit number 69. Mr. Leach, before you as Prosecutor exhibit 69, an aerial image, could you first of all please explain the source of that image and the date it was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is further photographs provided by the British Ministry of Defence in accordance with Rule 70. This photograph was taken on or about 11th October 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, noting the reservations of counsel, we would move to introduce Prosecutor's Exhibit 69 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, would you be so kind as to walk us through that particular photograph, explaining the salient features in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. You can see the main highway, which starts at the top of the photograph and goes to the bottom of the photograph. The road to Kiseljak would be in that direction, which would be south. The highway, there you travel north to Busovaca. If one turned off the highway, as you have seen from the aerial photograph and the stills and the video, this is now the village of Svinjarevo. Svinjarevo mosque is marked where this label is here. That was the building which actually still has the roof intact, but you have seen the still photographs of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would next tender a large aerial photograph as Prosecutor's exhibit number 70. Now, Mr. Leach, would you kindly first of all describe to the court the source of this photograph and the date it was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again a photograph provided by the British Ministry of Defence under Rule 70 and was taken on or about 11th October 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again subject to the reservations noted by counsel, your Honour, we would move to admit Prosecutor's exhibit number 70 into evidence. Mr. Leach, would you kindly walk us through the salient features that are depicted on Prosecutor's exhibit number 70?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. The main highway is again on the photograph here (indicating). If I start at the top of the photograph, the highway would move on to Kiseljak, which would be south. The mosque at Gromiljak is indicated with the label, of which you have just seen the video and the stills. The village of Gomionica, the video footage which first started at the bottom of the village, we commenced filming in this location here, and Gomionica travels up on to the hillside. This is the area of upper Gomionica and the main area of Gomionica here. Lower Gomionica is off the picture. Behrici is this area of buildings here. You would travel north to Busovaca. If you went down that road a couple of kilometres and turned right you would be into Svinjarevo, which was in the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would next tender as Prosecutor's exhibit number 71 another large aerial image. Mr. Leach, could you first of all start by testifying about who the provider was on this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was again given to the Prosecutor by the British Ministry of Defence under Rule 70 and again was taken on or about the 11th October 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, noting the reservations of counsel, we would move to introduce Prosecutor's exhibit number 71 into evidence. Mr. Leach, will you please orient us in respect of this particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, your Honours, the main highway between Busovaca and Kiseljak is here (indicating). The mosque at Gromiljak is here. This photograph has in effect moved south from the one you saw previously and now has lower Gomionica on it, which is this area here. It again has upper Gomionica to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, but isn't this somewhat like the preceding one, as far as Behrici? Didn't we see something like that already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You have seen something similar. The difference with this photograph is this includes all of Gomionica, including lower Gomionica, which was not on the previous photograph. At the bottom you will see labelled "Behrici" only a portion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So this is further north. This is further north then -- further south, rather. Further south?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And middle Gomionica is this area, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one more large photograph to complete this series. I can do it now or after the recess, whichever is the court's pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Then I would tender as Prosecutor's Exhibit 72, the last of the series of large aerial photographs in this sequence. Mr. Leach, what is the source of this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again, your Honours, the British Ministry of Defence provided under Rule 70 and again taken on or about 11th October 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, subject to again noting the reservation of counsel in respect of this exhibit, we would move to admit Prosecutor's exhibit number 72 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I thought that's what I said. If I misspoke, I apologise. It should be 72. Mr. Leach, will you kindly orient us in respect of Prosecutor's Exhibit 72?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. You saw three previous photographs of this area. This now covers the whole area. The main highway goes almost through the whole of the centre of the photograph. As indicated, the road to Kiseljak at the top, followed by Gromiljak mosque. Again on this photograph lower Gomionica isn't shown. Middle Gomionica and upper Gomionica are there, as is Behrici. If one goes down the photograph, that is in effect travelling north, there is Svinjarevo and Svinjarevo mosque. Over to the right, the top right-hand corner, is the location of the mosque at Hercezi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Leach. At this point, your Honour, it would be appropriate to take the recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will begin again at 5 o'clock. (4.35 pm) (Short break) (5.00 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume. Have the accused brought in, please. (Accused re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, do you think you will be finished by 6 o'clock?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: As you said. Yes, thank you. The floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Leach, I would like to turn your attention to the village of Visnjica and ask you, first of all, when did the HVO attack the village of Visnjica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was 18th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you start by looking at Exhibit 29D placing it on the ELMO and pointing out to counsel and the Trial Chamber the location of the village of Visnjica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Leach. Turning your attention to the 1991 census figures, what are the census figures for that particular village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population in 1991 was 942, of which 714 were Muslim, 1 Serb, 216 Bosnian Croats, 3 Yugoslav and 8 of another origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, what is the time and the distance from the Kiseljak Barracks to the village of Visnjica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's approximately 5.2 kms, which would take approximately eight minutes by car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you personally been to the village of Visnjica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe your observations of that particular village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This village is on a very low area of level ground off the main highway. It straddles approximately 2.5-3 kms from the main highway into the countryside. There are -- there is a lot of damage as you get deep into the village. The areas substantially nearer the highway for approximately 1.5-2 kms, there is limited damage in those areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Leach. Now, your Honours, I would like to tender Prosecutor's Exhibit 73, a photo album. Mr. Leach, would you first of all explain where these photographs are taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. These photographs were taken in Visnjica itself. They were taken on Thursday, 23rd May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally present when these photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do they accurately depict the damage to the structures that are identified in these particular photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would ask that Prosecutor's Exhibit 73 be admitted into evidence. Please, Mr. Leach, will you start by taking photograph Z1/601, placing it on the ELMO and explaining to counsel and the court what's depicted in that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a photograph of the mosque in Visnjica. This building is almost at the end of the village, one of the furthest points away from the main highway. Again, as in the other pictures of mosques that you have seen today, in the area located you can see where the minaret was stood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Would you now turn your attention to photograph Z1/604? What does that photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the inside of the mosque at Visnjica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now turn to photograph Z1/630? Mr. Leach, what does that photograph show?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a representative photograph of the type of damage you would see in the village of Visnjica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Would you reassemble the exhibit, please? Mr. Leach, I would like to turn your attention to the village of Rotilj. Let me ask you when did the HVO attack the village of Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on 18th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again turning your attention to Prosecutor's Exhibit 29D, would you put that on the ELMO and please orient counsel and the court as to where the village of Rotilj is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's between the 2 and 3 km mark on the left-hand side of the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Thank you kindly. Would you please refer to the 1991 census figures in respect of the village of Rotilj and describe them to the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1991 the total population was 472. 440 Bosnian Muslim; 17 Bosnian Croat; 1 Yugoslav; and 14 of other ethnic origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, have you been to the village of Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please just describe briefly the physical characteristics of the village of Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To get to Rotilj you would drive to Kiseljak town centre. You would leave the town centre heading north. Actually from the town centre itself you would take a left turn through a series of S-bends, and then you would drive along again a 2.5-3 km stretch of very narrow road. That stretch of road is the village of Rotilj. Again it's spread out and dispersed along a valley side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it in a valley itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the main it's in the valley itself, just on an elevated portion to the south of the valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What is the time and distance from the Kiseljak Barracks to the village of Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's approximately 4.6 kms. That's probably the furthest most points -- one of the furthest most points in the village. To get to that area would take approximately nine or ten minutes by car, because it's a very narrow road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following the attack on April 18th, 1993, what was the population fluctuations in the village of Rotilj, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's my understanding from my enquiries that the population in the village expanded substantially as a large number of Bosnian Muslim civilians were placed at the very furthest point in the village by the authorities of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Leach, we are going to be turning to another video tape. It's going to be segment 21. Let me ask you, first of all, to describe to the court and the counsel what will be seen on this particular piece of film?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This piece of film is an aerial clipping, which will give you an indication of the topography for the village of Rotilj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can we dim the lights, please, and play video tape 21? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the village travelling along from the main highway in a westerly direction. Sorry. My apologies. It's actually starting at the head of the village and travelling towards the main highway. There's an area in the village here where there's destroyed houses (indicating). Another section here of destroyed houses, and again the road now travels east towards Kiseljak town centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that that tape number 21 be admitted as Prosecutor's Exhibit 62/3. Now, Mr. Leach, I would like now to turn your attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mentioned that the inhabitants were pushed to the furthest side of the village of Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Were they chased from their homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What appears to have happened, your Honour, as a result of my enquiries, is that refugees from other villages that were attacked during this period were sent to Rotilj by the HVO. They were, in effect, detained. I wouldn't describe it as a camp or a similar kind of camp that you would have seen in other areas of Bosnia. However, there was a highly concentrated, large number of Bosnian Muslims from a variety of locations in Kiseljak Municipality, who were forced to stay and remain in Rotilj. It was an area where they were controlled, access was controlled in and out of the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: After the destruction they remain in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my last visit there, there were still people who were refugees from other villages within Kiseljak municipalities. They regard themselves as refugees even though they may -- because their homes are destroyed and they are not able to return to their former home and they are still in Rotilj or were when I was last there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender as Prosecutor's Exhibit 74 a large aerial photograph. Mr. Leach, let me ask you again the source of this photograph and the date the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The source of the photograph, your Honours, is the British Ministry of Defence provided under Rule 70. Photograph taken on or about 11th October 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, noting the reservations of counsel, we would move to introduce Prosecutor's Exhibit 74 into evidence. Please, Mr. Leach, would you orient us on this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is similar to the last photograph you saw, but takes you again further south to Kiseljak. You have the main highway from Busovaca heading south into Kiseljak town. If I keep my point at the top of the photograph, you have the town at the top (indicating). You have Kiseljak mosque, for which you have seen photographs. As I described, it's just on the roadside as you drive into the town. The road into Rotilj from the main town, and Rotilj village travels all along this road here. This is this area here where the majority of Muslim civilians were located after the attacks in April. For orientation purposes, you can then travel north down the main highway and again, as you have seen on previous photographs, you have the Gromiljak mosque almost in the centre of the picture. Then labelled for you, lower Gomionica, Gomionica, upper Gomionica, Behrici, and if one continued north on the road to Busovaca, again one would then turn right into the village of Svinjarevo, although, of course, that village is not on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Leach. I would like now to turn to another exhibit, which will be tendered as Prosecutor's exhibit number 75. Mr. Leach, referring to Prosecutor's Exhibit 75, was this another photograph that was provided by the British Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pursuant to Rule 70?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date that Prosecutor's Exhibit 75 was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On or about 11th October 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would move to admit into evidence Prosecutor's Exhibit 75, again recognising the reservation of counsel. Mr. Leach, please, would you orient us in respect of Prosecutor's Exhibit 75?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. On the bottom left-hand area is the highway from Busovaca to Kiseljak. This left-hand portion here is the main area of the town of Kiseljak. You have the Kiseljak mosque, as indicated by the label. Again one can see the road from Kiseljak centre through to Rotilj, the far end of Rotilj at the end of the valley. This portion here is a series of buildings. You have previously seen the aerial video. This is the Kiseljak Barracks. So, for example, to travel to Rotilj by foot, if one wanted to hike, for example, you could just hike over the hill, a short distance here. This is the crest of a hill, this area (indicating), probably a couple of kilometres. However, if you want to drive from Kiseljak Barracks to Rotilj by road in an ordinary vehicle, you would have to drive from the barracks along this road to the main road, through the town and then turn left to travel into Rotilj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Leach. Let me now tender Prosecutor's exhibit number 76. Mr. Leach, is Prosecutor exhibit number 76 a photograph that has been produced by the British Ministry of Defence pursuant to Rule 70?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again on or about 11th October 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would move to admit Prosecutor's Exhibit 76, subject to the reservations of counsel. Please, Mr. Leach, will you please describe what's depicted in Prosecutor's exhibit number 76?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In effect, your Honours, this is a blow-up of the upper part of the previous photograph. You have Kiseljak town or a portion of Kiseljak town here, a larger view of Kiseljak Barracks. Again the crest of a hill or hillside between the barracks and the village of Rotilj, and the road from Kiseljak town centre. The village of Rotilj starts in this area here and then continues through the valley to this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, we have been moving in date order in terms of attacks on villages. I would like to ask you when was the -- when did the HVO attack the village of Ocenici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on 19th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to return back to the Vitez municipality and ask you about the village of Gacice. Let me ask you, first of all, when was the village of Gacice attacked by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on 20th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please return to Prosecutor Exhibit 29C and place that on the ELMO and point out to the court and to counsel where the village of Gacice is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the 1991 census figures, could you tell us what the 1991 census figures were for the village of Gacice in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population was 632. Of those 325 were Bosnian Muslim, 2 Bosnian Serb, 264 Bosnian Croat, 24 Yugoslavian, 17 of other origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, from the Hotel Vitez, what is the time and the distance to the village of Gacice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's approximately 1.9 kms, possibly taking about three to four minutes by car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been to the village of Gacice, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let me ask you, Mr. Leach -- we are going to be turning to two more video tapes. First turn to video tape 11. Let me ask you -- it's only 35 seconds long, so it's going to be a very short video tape. What will we be seeing in that particular tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a video taken from the air, from a helicopter provided by IFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could we please dim the lights and play very slowly, if possible, tape number 11? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the village of Gacice, your Honours. To the right, which isn't in view, would be the chemical factory with the smoke stack, which you've seen on previous exhibits. So Gacice is to some effect on a hilltop overlooking the chemical factory. As the -- the chemical factory just came into shot at the end of the footage, just for a brief second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. President, would you like that brief clip played a second time? It was very short. I would ask that that slip be introduced as Prosecutor exhibit 34/14. Mr. Leach, while the lights remain dim, can you please tell us what we'll be seeing in tape number 12?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a static video, panoramic view, the photographer stood still, just moving round the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the village of Gacice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please could we play tape number 12? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you can see, the camera has focused in on the smoke stack. It's awkward to see but through the trees and the branches you can see the top red and white portions of the chemical plant smoke stack, which gives an indication of the village being above the actual chemical plant itself. Thereafter the photographer has just moved from left to right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that tape number 12 be -- I'm sorry. I thought it was over.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In effect what's happened now, there was a shortcut in the video, your Honours, but a full 360 degrees from this part of the village is now being done by the cameraman. There's another portion with the smoke stack from another position in the village. In the far distance you would have the town of Vitez, which would be lower than the village of Gacice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that tape number 12 be admitted as Prosecutor's 34/15. Next, your Honour, I would like to tender Prosecutor's exhibit number 77, which is a large aerial image. Mr. Leach, referring to Prosecutor's exhibit number 77, is this also a photograph that was submitted by the British Ministry of Defence under Rule 70?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the date that this particular image was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On or about 9th November 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been to the village of Gacice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, your Honour, I would move to admit Prosecutor's exhibit number 77, subject to the reservations of counsel. Mr. Leach, would you be so kind as to orient us as to this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. The top left-hand portion of the photograph is Vitez town, the southern edge of the town. The bottom right-hand corner is the village of Donja Vecerska. You have seen the opposite photograph of that earlier in my testimony. You then have above Donja Vecerska in the photograph in the valley below it the chemical plant. Again one can see the smoke coming from the chimney stack, the smoke stack. Then directly above the chemical plant on the photograph is the damaged portion, the destroyed portion of the village of Gacice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. How much was Vitez damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area of Stari Vitez, which is where the concentrated area of Muslim population was, had quite a large amount of damage, which can be seen from some of the 1994 aerial exhibits. The damage was still relevant then. There was less damage, although there was small areas of damage in the main area of Vitez town itself, which again is also apparent from the 1994 aerial photographs, some of those which have previously been submitted to you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would next tender Prosecutor's exhibit number 78, which is a photo album. Mr. Leach, Prosecutor's exhibit number 78, are those photographs that were taken in the village of Gacice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken on Monday, 27th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when those photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these photographs accurately depict the destruction that's shown in each of the images?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask the court to admit Prosecutor's exhibit number 78. Mr. Leach, would you kindly place photograph Z2/256 on the ELMO? Would you please explain to the court and to counsel what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a photograph in the village of Gacice itself. Again I should perhaps point out the smoke stack of the chemical plant, which again is a good indication that the village is on elevated ground, with the factory below it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, will you now turn to photograph Z2/250?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is representative, your Honours, of the damage in Gacice, as you have seen from the aerial photograph, the aerial video and the video taken from the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now take photograph Z2/254 and place that on the ELMO? Mr. Leach, what does that photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again that's just a good representative example of the condition of the houses in Gacice as taken in 1996 and as reflected in the aerial photograph in 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Leach. Could you reassemble that exhibit? Mr. Leach, now I would like to turn your attention to a later time period, June of 1993, an to the Kiseljak Municipality, specifically the village of Tulica. First of all, Mr. Leach, would you place Exhibit 29D on the ELMO? Would you kindly indicate to the council and court where the village of Tulica was indicated. If we could have a larger view of that, it would be helpful. Okay. Thank you very much, Mr. Leach. Turning to the 1991 census figures for the village of Tulica, what did they show?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total population 1991 was 280. Bosnian Muslim, 278; Bosnian Croat, 1; and other ethnic origin, 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, what is the time and the distance from the Kiseljak Barracks to the village of Tulica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's one where you would have to -- I have only been able to guestimate. I have not driven into Tulica. I would approximate it at 12 kms, maybe a little less. The reason I haven't driven there is I've been warned previously there may be mines in the area. So I've not actually been in the village itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The approximate distance you said approximately 12 kms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Not actually having physically had it measured or measured it myself, I can't say any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, we are going to turn to another film clip. It's film clip number 24. As you've done previously, would you please describe to the Trial Chamber and to counsel what will be seen on film clip number 24?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the village of Tulica photographed from the air from an IFOR helicopter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that photograph, that film clip taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 26th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can we have the lights dimmed, please, and roll film clip number 24? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The date was 27th May 1996. I apologise. This is the village of Tulica. Again it's reasonably well spread out, as one can see. It's on a hilltop. In effect, the helicopter travels around the village just to circle it. The majority of damage coming to the Eastern part of the village, overhead, below now, and then on the other side of the knoll of the hill: there one can see the considerable amount of damage to the houses there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that film clip number 24 be introduced and admitted as Prosecutor's Exhibit 62/4. One last question, Mr. Leach, about the village of Tulica. When did the HVO attack the village of Tulica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on 12th June 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, I would now like to turn your attention to the village of Han Ploca. When did the HVO attack the village of Han Ploca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was 13th June 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you again return to Prosecutor's Exhibit 29D, place it on the ELMO and orient the court and counsel to the location of the village of Han Ploca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, what is the time and the distance from the Kiseljak Barracks to the village of Han Ploca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's approximately 8.8 kms to Han Ploca, which would take approximately seven to eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Once again, Mr. Leach, we're going to turn to a video clip. It will be video clip number 23. Would you please explain to the court and counsel what they'll see in video clip number 23?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again an aerial view of Han Ploca taken from an IFOR helicopter on 27th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we have the lights dimmed, please, and play film clip number 23? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This section of the village is close to the main road but again is elevated on a hillside. The houses in this area are on the hill and were damaged, as could be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was perhaps our quickest film. Would the court care to see this brief clip replayed? All right. Your Honour, I would ask that film clip number 23 be admitted as Prosecutor's exhibit 62/5. Your Honour, my last exhibit which I would tender to the court today is exhibit number 79. It's a summary of distances and times. Mr. Leach, referring to Prosecutor's exhibit number 79, would you please inform us what that particular exhibit is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. As part of the investigation a member of the investigative team travelled throughout the area recording the distances as indicated here either by car or by foot. I have personally travelled these areas many, many times myself and have verified these distances, obviously subject to the difference in the calibration of an odometer on the car, the speedometer. We were not able to get a calibrated speedometer one would normally like for the distance by car. This is a very good representative sample of the distance by car of two various locations from the Hotel Vitez. As regards travelling those routes and distances and times, again I should stress that that is done under normal driving conditions with good road surface, without any delays or halts for any reason, a straight drive from A to B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The various locations that are described in there start from the Hotel Vitez, is that correct, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The first portion starts from the Hotel Vitez to locations in Vitez. The second portion deals with from travelling from Hotel Vitez to locations in Stari Vitez, the Muslim area. The third portion, on page 2, relates to other relevant locations, about which you will hear other witnesses testify, such as the BritBat Echelon Garage, the main Brit BatBase in Vitez, the Kiseljak Barracks. Thereafter page 2 continues with distances to the villages in the Vitez Municipality. Thereafter page 3 and page 4 deal with distances from the former JNA Barracks, which became the HVO headquarters in Kiseljak. Because the barracks in Kiseljak is not in the centre of the town, you will see two sets of figures, one for travelling from the barracks; the second set of figures for each location as if you travelled from the centre of Kiseljak town itself. So that gives you a balance between the two locations within Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that Prosecutor's Exhibit 79 be admitted into evidence. Your Honour, that concludes my examination of Mr. Leach. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that we will stop our work now. I remind you that we will resume on Friday at 10 o'clock and it will be devoted to the time that the Defence considers appropriate for his examination of Simon Leach and any possible questions that the judges might wish to ask. Under those circumstances the hearing is adjourned until Friday. (5.55 pm)

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until Friday morning at 10 o'clock
